summary: Dialogue tree runner: assign the UI references, call StartDialogue(rootNode).
overview: Walks a tree of DialogueNode assets and drives your dialogue UI: speaker name, portrait, body text and a button per available choice. It reuses toolkit pieces rather than duplicating them — TMPTypewriterEffect for the character-by-character reveal and Blackboard for conditional choices — and both are optional and null-checked, so it works with neither assigned.
useCases: An NPC conversation with branching choices, authored entirely as assets.
A linear cutscene or tutorial script with no branching at all.
Choices that only appear once a quest flag is set, via a Blackboard key.

params.why: Optional. Gates choices that declare a requiredBlackboardKey.
params.tuning: Leave unassigned if no choice is conditional — conditional choices are then simply always shown.

params.why: The root object shown while dialogue is running and hidden when it ends.
Label for the speaker's name. Blank on a node means a narrator line.
Optional portrait shown beside the speaker name.
The TMP_Text the line is written into.
Optional. If assigned, text reveals character by character instead of appearing at once.
params.tuning: Without it the line appears instantly, which is the right choice for a fast-forward or accessibility option.

params.why: Parent the choice buttons are spawned under.
An inactive template Button, cloned once per available choice.
params.tuning: Rebuilt from scratch on every node, so do not cache references to the spawned buttons.

gotchas.title: Choice buttons are destroyed and rebuilt per node
gotchas.body: Anything you wired onto a spawned button will not survive advancing. Wire behaviour to the choice data, not to the button instance.

gotchas.title: A node with no choices and no nextNode ends the conversation
gotchas.body: That is how you terminate a branch. An unintentionally empty nextNode looks identical to a deliberate ending.
